rv.q: Freeman's play isn't a drama of ideas: there's neither symmetrical engagement nor any immediate stakes.
Henner’s pitch-perfect performance captures the unflappable narcissism of an entire generation.
Ask poses interesting questions about generational political differences and wealth, framing them through a two-person showdown, the play never amps up the stakes enough to go all in on the drama.
Once the central conflict finally emerges, the production becomes considerably more compelling.

cn.t: Freeman's generational debate between an ACLU fundraiser and resistant donor offers a timely premise but proves frustrating in execution, with critics finding the 75-minute two-hander more intriguing in concept than delivery.
